one_star_reviews.text:
Ruined my portfolio, my relationship, and my will to live.

This app is a financial weapon of mass destruction wrapped in a sleek, minimalist UI. It doesn't just take your money; it systematically dismantles your entire life while sending you beautifully formatted push notifications.I deposited my entire house deposit because the slick onboarding process made me feel like an elite Wall Street macro-trader. Within forty-eight hours, the 50x leveraged CFDs on this app completely vaporised it. But the absolute peak of this digital nightmare happened on Tuesday night.I was at dinner with my partner, trying to explain how "temporary volatility" works, when my phone buzzed on the table. It was a push notification from the app. It didn't just notify me of a margin call; it lit up the screen with a bright red, animated banner that read: “Liquidation Complete! Better luck next time! ”My partner saw it, asked to see the account balance, and quietly left her half of the dinner money on the table. She packed her bags that night. I didn’t just lose my life savings; I got dumped because your app has a 120Hz refresh rate that makes financial ruin impossible to hide.When I messaged customer support crying and asking if there was a cooling-off period, a bot named "Finley" replied in three seconds with a link to an article on “Coping with Market Volatility through Mindfulness.”

one_star_reviews.text:
We visited this place on Sunday, the 9th, in the morning. The female staff member wearing a white T-shirt and glasses was extremely rude, unwelcoming, and appeared annoyed while taking our order. There was no greeting or friendly interaction at all, and she clearly doesn’t know how to speak to customers. Zero customer service from her. The other staff members were great, and the food was fantastic and very tasty, coffee was also excellent.

Update: This was definitely not about being asked to leave our trolley outside. We were completely fine with that and understood the safety reason. As clearly mentioned in my review, the issue was rude communication from the employee while taking our order. She was extremely annoyed because I couldn’t hear or understand her. You have security cameras, better review the footage before assuming. If trolley was the reason for my review, I would not have mentioned that the food was great and that the other staff were wonderful. The other employees were genuinely very sweet and helpful, with the exception of this one staff member. As a business, you should be open to feedback rather than making assumptions about what the review was actually about.

Very disappointing experience.

I booked a 9am appointment at the Burwood clinic two weeks in advance for a time-sensitive blood test. Before booking, I specifically confirmed multiple times that the clinic would be open.

I arrived this morning at 9am and waited for around 30 minutes, but there was no doctor, no reception staff and the clinic was completely closed. I also tried calling several times, with no answer.

I eventually called the Greenwich clinic and was told that Burwood is actually not open on Monday mornings. The frustrating part is that both the website and Google listing clearly state Monday–Friday, 9am–5pm.

I understand Burwood is a new clinic and there may be challenges, but accurate opening hours and basic communication should be the bare minimum. This caused completely avoidable stress, wasted time and extra travel, especially as my blood sample needed to reach the lab before the 1pm run.

Really disappointing experience. I hope the clinic updates its information and improves its communication so other patients don’t have to go through the same thing.

1 STAR — Absolutely disgraceful experience

If I could give zero stars, I would.

My experience with this support agency has been absolutely disgraceful. I was shown photos of the house beforehand that made it look clean, presentable and properly maintained. What I actually walked into was completely different. The property appeared to have been neglected for months and was in a shocking condition.

The house is regularly covered in mould, and you can report the problems over and over again and still nothing gets properly fixed. The swimming pool out the back is absolutely disgusting and has been left full of mould. This is not what anyone should be expected to live in.

The support is also basically non-existent. Workers come in for around 30 minutes a day and then leave. That’s supposed to be support? When you actually need help or something goes wrong, good luck trying to get anyone to answer.

The office phone is constantly switched off or unavailable. Trying to contact them and get an actual response is incredibly frustrating.

One of the worst parts of my experience was the washing machine. The support workers broke my washing machine, it was reported, and despite this, it still hasn’t been replaced or properly fixed. You’re just left to deal with the consequences.

What makes it even worse is being shown nice-looking photos of the property and then arriving to find something that looks completely different. People deserve to know exactly what they’re signing up for before moving into supported accommodation.

This has been an incredibly frustrating and disappointing experience. Poor communication, poor maintenance, inadequate support and unacceptable living conditions.

I would seriously think twice before accepting accommodation through this agency. Do not rely on the photos they show you — inspect the property yourself and ask exactly what support and maintenance you will actually receive.

Absolutely unacceptable.

Sharon Connell called me and said she was the most qualified and experienced at navigating this.

In my desperation I booked in and trusted.

Two thing were said after the session that were highly inappropriate. One in regards to what he did to me non consentually and her responses was "do you think that turned him on?" I went into fawn response and gaslit myself at the time of the session because I was in disbelief that had actually happened.

I've struggled with body image my whole life so to have they thrown in my face as that making me unlovable NEARLY pushed me over the edge.

I messaged Sharon Connell to both cancel our next session and requesting contact details of her supervision all to receive an email of "thank you for the learning experience, do you want to transfer to another person in the practice?" No. You said you are the best so that gives me little faith around anyone else being any better.

If someone can contact me, they would be appreciated.

The session was recorded. I have the emails.

one_star_reviews.text:
We were disappointed with the level of detail in our pre-purchase inspection report, particularly regarding the roof.

The report identified a few cracked/chipped tiles and recommended re-bedding loose tiles. The wording indicated a relatively minor issue. However, after purchasing the property, three independent roofing companies inspected the roof and all advised that the whole roof required maintenance to ensure it was watertight.

There is a significant difference between maintaining a few affected tiles and maintaining the whole roof, particularly in terms of the extent, cost and urgency of the work.

When we raised this with Daniel Simpson, he stated that the roof had been assessed based on its “visible condition at the time.” The weather was fine and there were no apparent obstructions preventing a proper inspection. This left us questioning whether the roof was assessed thoroughly enough, or whether Daniel had sufficient knowledge and experience to recognise and communicate the extent of the required maintenance.

We relied on the report when purchasing the property and subsequently incurred an unexpected extra cost for roof maintenance after purchase.

Our refund request was declined due to the 60-day period. Regardless, we remain dissatisfied with the quality and level of detail of the inspection and, based on our experience, would not use or recommend this service.

I was referred to Dr Mohan by my gynaecologist for what I understood to be a simple yes-or-no question. I was told that Dr Mohan would not see patients without private health insurance.

My insurance waiting period ends in December, and I do not require hospital admission, just an outpatient consultation. Medicare can provide rebates for eligible outpatient specialist consultations, and private hospital cover is a separate matter.

I was disappointed to hear that Dr Mohan won’t even do an outpatient appointment which has nothing to do with private health. Patients deserve clear information about their options when seeking specialist advice, rather than feeling that access to care depends on having private health insurance.

I’m sharing my experience so future patients know that Dr Mohan will not see anyone unless they have hospital cover even if it’s a yes or no question or outpatient appointment.

one_star_reviews.text:
Something needs to be done about our Emergency Departments

Last night I took my friend to the Emergency Department because she was experiencing a severe burning sensation in her stomach. We ended up waiting for approximately 12 hours, which I found extremely distressing.

During that time, I asked one of the nurses if my friend could have some Panadol for her pain. Unfortunately, it never arrived, and eventually I had to go and get some myself.

I also approached the staff approximately three times to ask how much longer we might have to wait. Each time, we were told it would be “another three hours.” I understand that Emergency Departments are extremely busy and that patients must be treated according to the seriousness of their condition. I also understand that staff are under enormous pressure.

However, as a member of the public, it is incredibly frustrating to sit there for hour after hour, watching staff chatting and laughing while patients are waiting for care.

I really believe the WA Labor Government needs to do more to address the pressure on our Emergency Departments and reduce these lengthy waiting times.

We keep hearing about Urgent Care Clinics as an alternative to Emergency Departments, but some of these services are not available when people actually need them, particularly after hours.

If we are being encouraged to use Urgent Care Clinics instead of Emergency Departments, then surely they need to be properly accessible, including during evenings, nights and weekends.

People should not have to sit in pain for 10–12 hours before receiving medical attention.

I am not blaming individual nurses or doctors who are working under enormous pressure. I am saying that the system needs to be improved.

Our healthcare system needs more resources, better access to after-hours care and a serious plan to reduce Emergency Department waiting times.

This is about making sure people can receive the care they need, when they need it.

Because what happened I am very unhappy with the way my treatment with my Dr Palaniappan ended. My treatment was suddenly discontinued after I made an error in relation to my medication...and was not asked how I was feeling or WHY I did what I did. Isn't that why we go to Psych. as we are not well and don't necessarily do things right and we do pay for our own treatment as well. We are trying to get help.

At the time, we were still in the process of finding a suitable medication dosage for me. I was therefore surprised that I was asked when I wanted my next appointment to be, rather than being ADVICED when I should be reviewed as part of the ongoing medication management process. I relied on my psychiatrist's professional guidance regarding appropriate follow-up while my medication and dosage were still being adjusted.

What concerns me most is that when my treatment was discontinued, I was not provided with a referral or a clear transition plan to another psychiatrist so that my treatment could continue safely. If Dr felt that my needs were complex or outside her particular area of expertise or experience, I believe she could have referred me to a psychiatrist with greater experience in managing complex cases and medication management. Instead, I was left to find another psychiatrist myself while also dealing with the effects of severe withdrawals suddenly stopping my medication.

I accept that I made an error in relation to my medication. However, I do not believe that this removed the need to consider my ongoing wellbeing and continuity of care. I needed appropriate medical support and a safe transition of care, rather than being left without psychiatric treatment.

I felt abandoned as a patient at a time when I needed professional support. I have serious concerns about  appropriate continuity of care and duty of care were provided when my treatment was terminated.

If I could leave no stars, I would. Dr. Maia McFadden found my son to be in the "too hard basket" I guess and couldn't be bothered to try and treat him or help him.  We wasted nothing but a lot of time and a lot of money on her. My son's mental health has now exponentially worsened thanks to her. She just decided she no longer has "capacity" for him. Don't take on a patient, make them go through all of the traumatic history etc etc etc and then drop them without a word or a consideration. I even begged her for just one more appointment, but she didn't even bother to reply. Utterly unprofessional, disrespectful and deeply, deeply disappointing.

I’m extremely disappointed with my experience at this salon.

The person who cut my hair was the manager. Before the haircut, I spent around five minutes trying to clearly explain the type of bob I wanted and also showed her reference photos. Unfortunately, I don’t think there was a clear understanding of what I was asking for.

She used thinning/texturising scissors very heavily through the lower sections of my hair, removing far too much volume. The ends were left extremely thin, uneven and wispy, and the overall shape of the haircut is very irregular. Instead of having a clean, structured bob, the bottom of my hair now looks sparse and sticks out awkwardly.

I tried to live with the haircut for the past two to three months, but I have remained unhappy with it. I went back on Saturday simply to ask for some advice and to see whether anything could be done before booking another haircut. Unfortunately, the manager was very dismissive, impatient and quite rude in the way she spoke to me. I did not feel that she was interested in listening to my concerns or helping me find a solution.

I also found communication difficult throughout my experience. I understand that English may not be everyone’s first language, but as a customer I still expect reasonable communication, patience and respect, particularly when I am trying to explain exactly what I want before a haircut.

Overall, I really regret coming here. I wish I had gone somewhere else, as it will now take months for the overly thinned sections of my hair to grow out properly.

This provider’s practices are extremely concerning. I strongly recommend looking closely at their accommodation rules and the additional clauses they appear to insert into their agreements. The overall approach comes across as being driven by financial gain rather than genuine participant choice, control and wellbeing.
There are serious concerns around special terms in their agreements that appear to charge participants for support hours that have not actually been delivered. Even more concerning is the apparent restriction on a participant’s ability to change support providers while living in one of their properties. This effectively removes genuine choice and control and can leave people, particularly those experiencing homelessness or housing instability, in a position where they feel they have no option but to accept support from the same provider offering the accommodation.

I have personally had a client turned away because he could not commit to receiving 20 hours of support per week from Brave Minds. As a result, he was unable to move into their property. Given that this was a housing opportunity for someone who was homeless, it is extremely concerning that access to accommodation appears to have been conditional on accepting a specified level of support from the provider.

This raises serious questions about participant choice and control, conflicts of interest, and whether these practices are consistent with NDIS requirements and standards. At the very least, I believe these arrangements warrant close scrutiny by the relevant regulatory bodies.

Yesterday, while waiting to be seen at APM, I witnessed an interaction that left me extremely disappointed and disgusted, particularly because I have previously worked for APM myself.

A woman arrived for her appointment and was clearly struggling to walk. When it was her turn, she was called up to see a consultant. As she made her way over, visibly struggling and walking with difficulty, the consultant remained standing at her desk with what appeared to be a very dismissive and unpleasant expression. At no point did the consultant acknowledge that the woman was struggling or ask whether she needed assistance.

What happened after the appointment was even more concerning.

As the woman was leaving, she continued to struggle to walk, stopping every few steps to hold her knee. There were approximately 10–15 consultants in the office that day. A group of consultants gathered around the desk where the woman had been sitting and watched her struggle while talking amongst themselves. Despite having numerous people around, not one person got up to check whether she was okay, ask if she needed help, or even show basic concern for her wellbeing.

Eventually, I felt I could no longer sit there and watch. I got up, approached the woman myself and asked if she was okay. What shocked me even further was that, while I was doing this, the consultants simply watched.

Then, a consultant behind me called out to the woman and said, “If you can’t walk, go to the hospital,” in what I found to be an extremely rude and dismissive tone.

This experience was incredibly upsetting to witness. Regardless of someone’s circumstances, disability, health, or reason for attending an appointment, they deserve to be treated with dignity, compassion and basic human decency.

Having previously worked for APM, this was particularly disappointing. Customer service is not simply about completing appointments or following procedures  it is also about treating people with respect and recognising when someone may need assistance.

I sincerely hope this incident is taken seriously and used as an opportunity to reflect on the level of care and compassion being shown to clients. If staff are unable or unwilling to demonstrate basic human decency towards someone who is visibly struggling, serious consideration needs to be given to the customer service standards being upheld.

Do better, APM.

No reception desk on the premises, just a printed sign stating to take a seat and that somebody would 'check in as soon as possible'. 13:40 and somebody appeared with a post-it note, jotting down names of the people waiting. -Rather interesting that since I posted my review (and it being the only review of her services at the time!) that Victoria felt the need to solicit other clients to write positive reviews. This would indicate that this “professionals” own failure schema is in full force. The fact is, she did fail and since this review, I have also been contacted by another former client in which she was treated similarly to I. These contrived positive reviews that did not exist before I posted mine, are a further indication of how poor this psychologist's boundaries and her ethics actually are.-

I worked with Vicki for approximately 5.5 years in long-term therapy, much of which centred on attachment, relational safety, and repair. Over time, a strong therapeutic alliance was intentionally developed, with the understanding that trust, consistency, and the capacity to work through rupture were foundational to addressing complex developmental trauma.

I was not an uncomplicated client. I came into therapy with significant trauma, and that presented in complex and, at times, challenging ways. However, I was consistently engaged in the process, highly self-reflective, and committed to the work. I did not avoid accountability.

It is within that context that the termination of therapy must be understood. The ending was abrupt, not collaboratively planned, and did not reflect the principles of gradual transition and relational repair that had been central to the work over many years. In attachment-focused therapy, the ending is part of the treatment. To have it handled in this way was not only distressing but clinically damaging, as it directly undermined the framework the therapy was built upon. The stated reason for termination was unresolved countertransference and its impact on the Vicki’s physical health. While countertransference itself is not unusual, its management is a core professional responsibility. It is expected to be addressed through supervision and appropriate professional support. It also should not ever come as a “surprise” to a client.

Being told directly that my therapist’s physical health had been affected by working with me placed a significant and inappropriate emotional burden on me as the client.  I This was particularly impactful given the level of care and trust that had developed within the therapeutic relationship. It introduced an implicit sense of responsibility for her wellbeing, which is not appropriate within a therapeutic context and it was deeply distressing to know that this occurred. Even I, as the client, would never dump that emotional burden on another, and certainly not in a professional space.

In addition my autism diagnosis was not identified during the course of therapy. This had significant implications for how my experiences were conceptualised, particularly in relation to autistic burnout and the interaction and scaffolding between neurodivergence and trauma. A neuro-affirming formulation would likely have led to a more accurate understanding of my presentation and I thought Vicki had the capacity and the courage to see this nuance in me.

What remains most difficult is the level of trust that had been established over time. The therapeutic relationship was positioned as a space where rupture could be repaired and where I was consistently told that I was worthy of care, understanding, and consistency. The manner in which this ended was not aligned with those principles and constituted a significant breach of that trust. I believed Vicki and considered her to be sincere and I felt like I was in good hands being how informed, intelligent and progressive she was about differing modalities and I truly believed I was in safe hands with her. I was wrong.

I am a person who can often be reactive so I have sat with this for six months, not acting or wanting to be spiteful so this review is considered and will close the final chapter for me.

Save yourself the heartache and choose another “psychologist”. I trusted Vicki as a therapist and as a decent human being and I believe she truly let me down.

More times has the clinic been closed because the collector ‘isn’t working today’ than they are actually open.

I have been trying for months to get my partner to fast to actually get his blood test done and this morning, Friday 16th October, we go in there when they are supposedly ’open’ only to be told yet again ‘oh, she’s not working today, go to Gooding Drive’. So thanks heaps to the workers of QML Emerald Lakes for once again failing to turn up to work and making all my efforts of the past months a waste of time. Too bad if there’s actually a problem because it’s going to take more time to convince him to start again and go somewhere else.

Needless to say, I would NOT recommend this clinic.

one_star_reviews.text:
I attended this clinic for a relatively short period when I was exploring the possibility of having a baby on my own. At the time, I didn’t know what my natural fertility was like or whether I would have difficulty becoming pregnant, which was why I sought professional advice in the first place.

What I found particularly upsetting was the repeated emphasis on my age. I was made to feel that I was already too old to freeze my eggs and that IVF was essentially my only realistic chance of becoming a mother, using donor sperm. I left those appointments feeling devastated, hopeless and as though my opportunity to have a child had already passed me by.

I was also extremely disappointed to later discover that “polycystic follicular disease” had been documented in my medical history. This was never discussed with me or explained to me during my appointments, and I have subsequently been told that this diagnosis does not appear to be accurate. Unfortunately, it has followed me into my pregnancy records, and I now find myself having to explain or address it at midwifery appointments.

My experience ultimately turned out very differently from the picture that had been presented to me. At age 40, I became pregnant naturally and very easily.

I completely understand that fertility does decline with age and that healthcare professionals have a responsibility to discuss those statistics and potential risks with patients. However, there is an enormous difference between providing realistic, evidence-based information and making a woman feel that pregnancy after a certain age is virtually hopeless.

Women deserve balanced information about fertility, including the limitations of population statistics and the fact that individual fertility can vary considerably. Women over 35 should not automatically be made to feel that their chances of becoming mothers have disappeared.

The way fertility information is communicated matters. For someone who desperately wants a child, repeatedly being told that they are “too old” can be incredibly distressing. I hope greater consideration is given to how these conversations are handled in the future so that women receive honest information without unnecessarily having their hope taken away.

one_star_reviews.text:
My mum attended this clinic this morning for a blood test, and unfortunately, the experience was extremely disappointing.

There have been quite a few new staff members recently, and sadly, the level of friendliness, understanding and empathy has not been the same as it was previously. The staff who were here before were absolutely amazing, and their care and compassion were a big reason we continued coming back. Unfortunately, after today’s experience, we will now need to look elsewhere, which has caused my mum a great deal of distress.

My mum has difficult venous access due to a chronic health condition and has always experienced difficulties with having blood taken. We made an effort to explain her situation and what would be required before her appointment, but unfortunately, we did not feel that our concerns were taken seriously.

During the appointment, the staff member who performed the blood draw was unfortunately not friendly, accommodating or empathetic towards my mum’s situation. We completely understand that blood tests can sometimes be difficult and that staff have challenging days, but when dealing with patients who have ongoing health issues and genuine difficulties with procedures, a little patience and understanding can make an enormous difference.

If you have easy veins and generally have no difficulty having blood taken, you may have a perfectly fine experience here. However, based on our experience, I unfortunately would not recommend this clinic to someone who has difficult venous access or requires a little extra care and patience during blood tests.

I genuinely wish this experience had been different. This review is not written out of malice, but out of genuine disappointment and sadness at the way my mum was treated. We had previously had such positive experiences here, which makes today particularly upsetting.

In healthcare, empathy goes a long way. Patients are often already dealing with enough, and being treated with a little kindness, patience and understanding can make a difficult experience so much easier.

After 5 years as a tenant in a property managed by Frank Dowling, I've had a handful of property managers, the first of which was probably the best experience I have ever had with a property manager. As someone who typically likes to fly under the radar, I have always paid my rent on time, requested very few repairs and aside from the usual property inspections, had very little contact with them.

Unfortunately, the last 3 months have been the worst experience I have ever had with a property manager in my 10 years as a renter. Things that should have been easy, have been stressful and taken up far more mental energy than is necessary.

I had already requested a couple of small maintenance issues when I received a 'friendly reminder' text message about a significant rental increase taking place the following month which I had heard nothing about prior to this. From there, I spent the next month consistently chasing updates on both the rent negotiation and the repairs. Despite promises to improve communication, I was still the one initiating every follow up. The significant rent increase went ahead while maintenance issues remained unresolved and in some cases unacknowledged.

While the repairs did eventually go ahead after a few prompts, I am still living with a makeshift repair on my shower that has been in place for over two months. My attempts to find out whether this is permanent or whether there are plans to complete the work have been ignored.

As someone who is incredibly uncomfortable making a fuss, this whole process has been deeply unpleasant. I have held off on any public review for a long time hoping not only that things would improve, but also nervous that having to continue to chase and make a pest of myself may put my living situation at risk. Frank Dowling's own website describes their team as dedicated to 'respect, reliability and responsiveness.' In my experience, I have seen none of those three things.

one_star_reviews.text:
Dr Jameel Ashraf has been both my GP and my son’s GP. In relation to my son’s care, both my partner and I have been very happy with Dr Ashraf and considered him to be excellent.
Unfortunately, my own experience regarding a more complex and nuanced medical issue was very different.

Dr Ashraf speaks fluent English, but I left the consultation with the clear impression that he had not fully understood the issue I was trying to explain. During the appointment, he acknowledged that he was not clear about what I was describing. What concerned me most was the limited number of investigative or clarifying questions asked to improve that understanding. The questions that were asked did not appear to align with the central issue I was explaining, leaving me feeling that there was a significant disconnect.

Despite this acknowledged lack of clarity, an important decision was made regarding my medical treatment. When I later asked for the reasoning behind that decision, I did not receive an explanation that I found clear, coherent or responsive to the concerns I had raised.

Dr Ashraf then referred me to his colleague at the same practice, Dr Syed Ali, for a second opinion. Unfortunately, my experience was similar. I felt that Dr Ali relied heavily on Dr Ashraf’s notes rather than independently exploring my history and circumstances through detailed questioning. I therefore left feeling that my situation had still not been properly understood.

I have since secured another doctor who listened carefully, asked detailed investigative questions and made a genuine effort to understand the complete situation. After doing so, that doctor reached the opposite clinical conclusion to Dr Ashraf and Dr Ali.

It would be unfair and inaccurate for me to claim that either doctor is generally a bad doctor. As noted, our experience with Dr Ashraf treating my son has been very positive. However, based on my personal experience, I do not believe either doctor demonstrated an adequate level of investigation or comprehension when dealing with my complex presentation.

I also understand that this practice does not currently use HotDoc’s patient-review system. I would encourage the practice to consider proactively inviting patients to provide honest feedback about their consultations. A broader and more representative body of patient feedback may help the practice identify areas in which individual doctors are performing well, as well as areas where further communication, comprehension or consultation training may be beneficial. This would give the practice a clearer picture of patient experiences rather than relying only on feedback from the small number of patients who independently decide to post public reviews.

My central concern is not simply that the doctors initially misunderstood me. Misunderstandings can occur, particularly with complicated medical matters. My concern is that significant decisions were made despite that lack of understanding, without sufficient clarifying questions being asked first.

This review reflects my own experience. I genuinely hope the practice, Dr Ashraf and Dr Ali take the feedback constructively and place greater emphasis on ensuring that complex patient concerns are properly understood before important clinical decisions are made.

I cannot recommend this company based on my experience. I paid $300 for a professional whole-house pest inspection and specifically raised concerns about a hollow section of my door frame. I was told it was caused by “ants” and that there was nothing to worry about. Three months later, I discovered that it was termite activity, and the damage had significantly worsened. If you have any concerns about termites, I strongly recommend getting a second opinion rather than relying solely on their inspection.

I first noticed that part of my door frame sounded hollow and immediately became concerned that it could be termite damage. I paid $300 for a whole-house pest inspection and specifically pointed out the condition of the door frame to the technician.

Despite my concerns, I was told that it was “ants” and that I did not need to worry. Although I had my doubts, I chose to trust the professional advice I had paid for.

Three months later, the hollow area had become significantly worse, and the affected area had clearly expanded. I was able to pull two insects that appeared to be termites from a crack in the door frame.

I contacted customer service, and they acknowledged that it was termite activity and sent the same technician back to address the issue.

What I found particularly concerning was that the technician continued to insist that there had only been ants during the first inspection. He then claimed that the termites had appeared three months later because “ants can bring termites into the house.”

I found this explanation extremely difficult to accept.

When I first suspected termites, I acted promptly and paid for a professional inspection specifically because I wanted to identify and deal with the problem before it became more serious. I relied on the technician’s professional assessment and was told not to worry. Three months were then lost, and the damage has now become significantly worse.

I paid $300 for professional expertise and expected a specific concern I raised to be properly assessed. Instead, I feel that the incorrect assessment and lack of professionalism have left me in a significantly worse position.

Based on this experience, I cannot recommend this company.

one_star_reviews.text:
My mum attended this clinic this morning for a blood test, and unfortunately, the experience was extremely disappointing.

There have been quite a few new staff members recently, and sadly, the level of friendliness, understanding and empathy has not been the same as it was previously. The staff who were here before were absolutely amazing, and their care and compassion were a big reason we continued coming back. Unfortunately, after today’s experience, we will now need to look elsewhere, which has caused my mum a great deal of distress.

My mum has difficult venous access due to a chronic health condition and has always experienced difficulties with having blood taken. We made an effort to explain her situation and what would be required before her appointment, but unfortunately, we did not feel that our concerns were taken seriously.

During the appointment, the staff member who performed the blood draw was unfortunately not friendly, accommodating or empathetic towards my mum’s situation. We completely understand that blood tests can sometimes be difficult and that staff have challenging days, but when dealing with patients who have ongoing health issues and genuine difficulties with procedures, a little patience and understanding can make an enormous difference.

If you have easy veins and generally have no difficulty having blood taken, you may have a perfectly fine experience here. However, based on our experience, I unfortunately would not recommend this clinic to someone who has difficult venous access or requires a little extra care and patience during blood tests.

I genuinely wish this experience had been different. This review is not written out of malice, but out of genuine disappointment and sadness at the way my mum was treated. We had previously had such positive experiences here, which makes today particularly upsetting.

In healthcare, empathy goes a long way. Patients are often already dealing with enough, and being treated with a little kindness, patience and understanding can make a difficult experience so much easier.

My Experience

I am 73 years old, and this review is based on my own experience with this practice.

For almost a year, I have been unable to comfortably wear my dentures because they have caused ongoing soreness, irritation and bruising around my gums. As a result, I have struggled to eat normally and have had to rely heavily on soft foods and liquids. This has also affected my confidence, social life and overall quality of life.

My son has supported me throughout this process and has communicated my concerns to the practice on my behalf. We have made genuine efforts to give the practice opportunities to assess the problems and find a suitable solution, but unfortunately the issues have continued.

I was particularly disappointed when I was offered a $1,300 refund for the reline on the condition that my negative Google reviews be removed and proof of their removal be provided.

I do not consider this an appropriate resolution to what I have experienced. A refund does not undo almost a year of suffering, discomfort, difficulty eating, loss of confidence and the impact this situation has had on my social life and overall wellbeing. Nor does it address my concerns about the treatment I received or the ongoing problems I have experienced with my dentures.

I am sharing my experience so that others can make an informed decision. I believe customers should be able to share their genuine experiences openly and honestly.

one_star_reviews.text:
This morning, July 11, 2026, I accompanied one of my clients to Jingzong Temple for a group practice session. I accompany this client here almost every Saturday, and we have lunch together at midday.

I used to have lunch at the temple with everyone, too. However, I eventually began to feel uncomfortable with the dining atmosphere, especially because of the way some volunteers treated visitors. I no longer eat the food there and only have a cup of soup.

After finishing my first cup of soup today, I saw that more than ten cups were still left. A Chinese-speaking female volunteer who was serving the soup and food was asking other people, “Would you like another cup?” She always looks stern, and I have never seen her smile. So I politely said that I would like another cup as well.

To my surprise, she said bluntly, “You don’t get one. Just because someone else wants one, you want one too.” Her tone was very unfriendly, and I felt deeply upset. I couldn’t understand what I had done to offend her, as we don’t know each other. It also made me feel that I was being treated differently.

This was not the first time. On the many occasions I have accompanied my client here, whenever this Chinese-speaking volunteer has been serving the food, she has consistently been cold and impatient with me, while treating other people differently. I completely understand that the temple may have rules about serving food. If the rule is that each person may only have one cup of soup, I can accept that. She only needed to explain it politely. Enforcing a rule and treating visitors with respect and courtesy are not mutually exclusive.

I’m writing this review not because I couldn’t get an extra cup of soup, and it’s not as if I have no food to eat and need to rely on her. I hope the temple will pay attention to the volunteers’ attitudes towards visitors. I believe that people who volunteer at a temple do so because they want to support the temple and learn about Buddhism. For that very reason, they should treat everyone who visits with compassion, fairness and respect. Even when rules need to be enforced, they can be explained gently and politely, rather than making someone feel singled out or looked down upon.

I sincerely hope the temple will take this matter seriously, so that people who come to learn about Buddhism can experience not only the solemnity of the ceremonies, but also the compassion, inclusiveness and kindness that Buddhism teaches.

Warning to All Business Owners: Unethical and Retaliatory Practices
​I am writing this review to warn other business owners about the deeply unethical and retaliatory practices of Digital Reality Australia.
​Recently, I received a cold call from their representatives trying to pitch their services to my company. I politely declined, making it clear that we were not interested. However, shortly after turning down their offer, a negative review was posted against my business from a private Google account.
​A Coordinated Pattern of Retaliation
​Unfortunately, my experience is not an isolated incident. After speaking with other local business owners who have also been hit with sudden negative reviews, a disturbing pattern emerged:

​The Call-Review Cycle: Several business owners confirmed that they had also recently received a sales call from this entity (or similar operators connected to them) and politely declined their services, only to be slapped with an unprovoked negative review a few days later.
​Anonymous Accounts: These reviews are deliberately being left using private, anonymous Google accounts to hide their tracks.
​The Follow-Up Pitch: The ultimate goal of this manipulative tactic appears to be coercion—they attempt to strong-arm and pressure business owners into hiring them after damaging their online reputation.

​Phantom Contact Information
​When I attempted to follow up and address this unprofessional behavior, I found that none of their contact channels work:
​The Australian contact number they use to call businesses is completely unresponsive or goes straight to a disconnected/fake line when you try to call them back.
​While they list an Australian address, their operations and main lines trace elsewhere, leaving local businesses with zero accountability and no way to reach a legitimate representative

one_star_reviews.text:
Went into Myer for clothes and asked a young guy wearing a Myer badge for help in the men's shoe section. He marched me straight to one rack and, every time I asked about anything else, dragged me back: "these are the best." Trusting the badge, I bought a $350 pair of white leather shoes. Aquila, as it happened.

Came back to collect them, asked about a different pair, and got: "I can't help with that, you'll have to find someone else." An Aquila rep the entire time. No Aquila badge, no disclosure, nothing. Just a Myer lanyard and a sales pitch disguised as impartial advice. I've got no issue with brand reps. I've got a serious issue with being funnelled into a $350 purchase by someone posing as a neutral store employee. It's deceptive, it's grubby, and it's a shocking look for both Aquila and Myer.

And the shoes themselves? Two wears. Two. The leather is already splitting away from the sole. $350 for footwear that's structurally failing before the first week is out. Apparently the only thing Aquila is good at is the hard sell.

Sneaky to sell, shoddy to wear. Avoid this company.

one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely disappointed with our experience at KFC tonight.

We went into the store at around 6pm and ordered a Giant Feast. We were told there would be a 20-minute wait. Frustrating during peak dinner time, but we understood things happen and agreed to wait in the car.

At around the 15-minute mark, we watched a staff member take a Giant Feast out to a waiting drive-through car. A couple of minutes later, another feast order was taken out to another drive-through customer.

I went back inside to check on our order and the younger female staff member, who was apologetic, told us they only had 7 pieces of chicken left because drive-through had taken the rest, meaning we’d now have to wait ANOTHER 10 minutes. During the conversation, she also explained that drive-through was the priority.

This is where our frustration really kicked in. We’d already paid and patiently waited nearly 20 minutes, yet our order was being pushed back while drive-through customers continued receiving the available chicken.

We asked for a refund. The manager was quick to tell us refunds were cash only, which was completely fine. What wasn’t fine was her attitude. When we explained our frustration about watching drive-through customers receive feast orders, she dismissively told us we didn’t know what they had ordered. Except we DID — we clearly heard the staff member say “Giant Feast” when delivering one of them.

There was no genuine apology, no acknowledgement of our frustration and absolutely no care shown that we’d waited nearly 20 minutes and were now leaving without dinner.

We understand restaurants get busy and waits happen. That wasn’t the issue. Being told drive-through was the priority after we’d already paid and waited, followed by the manager’s dismissive attitude, was the issue.

A simple apology and some basic customer service would have completely changed this situation. Instead, we left angry, disappointed and without dinner.

We found and began working with Iain to build our home. We said out budget was $750,000 and Ian was kind, polite and filled us with confidence that he could deliver a beautiful, well built home for that.
Iain was with us from day one of the design process, attending design meetings and providing feedback at every stage, directing us on what was and wasn't within our budget; many of our design decisions came from him telling us what we could and couldn't afford.
Several months into the project and after countless hours of work Iain delivered to us the budget. It was $752,000.... + $100,000 of essential, excluded extras (lighting, taps and sinks, cabinetry for the kitchen and bathrooms etc.). We were initially reeling from the price jump but agreed that we could move forward. The exclusions would bring the overall price down, so he was working hard to meet our budget, after all. A few weeks later he presented us with an "updated" costing which was now $930,000 + the extras so well over a $1M build. At this point we abandoned the project. Our disappointment in this whole process is that we believe early on in the project Iain knew he could not deliver the project for the budget he initially said and he kept this information from us, allowing us to spend thousands unnecessarily in design and engineering costs for a project he knew he could not deliver. I'm sure Iain could build you a beautiful, premium house as long as you have a premium budget.
